extracted.intended_audience: students, writers, and readers studying Indian aesthetics, drama, and creative writing (introductory level)
extracted.subtask_description: A concise summary and analysis of the classical Indian Rasa theory as applied to drama and performance, explaining the components (Bhavas, Vibhavas, Anubhavas, Vyabhicaribhavas) and the principal Rasas to inform creation and critique of aesthetic experience. Useful for writers, actors, and literature students seeking to evoke or analyze Rasa in art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goal of drama / Rasa Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Entertainment (in drama/performance) is expected to evoke Rasa or joy (artistic) but that is not the primary goal. The primary goal is instead to create parallel life in front of the audience to experience a sense of one’s own (i.e. Consciousness, spiritual and moral question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on drama producing a mirrored, intensified life for the audience so they attain insight/consciousness; Rasa is a vehicle for moral/spiritual reflection rather than mere amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama as synthesis of all arts (Bharatamuni)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bharatamuni believes that the dramatic form of aesthetic experience is the most perfect fruition of aesthetic activity because drama is the synthesis of all arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or evaluating drama, consider how multiple arts (poetry, music, gesture, stagecraft) integrate to produce the Rasa experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of Rasa (undefinable aesthetic emotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasa means aesthetics, juice, essence, taste in performance. Rasa is an undefinable realization and intense feelings with detachment; the flavor or aesthetic emotion; the soul of poetry. It is the impression created on the mind of the sympathetic audience by the expressions of Bhavas and it’s experienced by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rasa cannot be fully defined by words; it is an aestheticized emotion felt in the artistic context (not common life). Effective art evokes this distinct, detached delight in spectators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological foundation: primary emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasa’s foundation is laid upon a particular view of psychology that holds our personality and according to which a few primary emotions live in the conscious and subconscious state of our being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These primary emotions are the raw material for aesthetic transformation; creators should work with these deep, often subconscious dispositions to elicit Rasa. The theory later expands the set of primary emotions beyond the original eight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sthaibhavas (permanent or dominant moods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sthaibhavas are the permanent or dominant moods. They are 8 in number: Rati (love), Hasya (humorous), soka (sorrow), krodha (anger), utsaha (enthusiasm), bhaya (fear), jugupsa (disgust) and vismaya (wonder). Later on, passiveness was added by Abhinavgupta and Anandvardhana.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sthaibhavas are the basis of Rasa, supreme among all Bhavas (49 in number). They constitute the principal theme of a composition and run through emotions like a garland; transient states feed and strengthen them to help them emerge as Rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vibhavas (situations/stimuli that evoke Sthaibhavas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vibhavas are the situations which are responsible to bring out Sthaibhavas. Vibhavas have two aspects - Alambana and Uddipana. The person in whose mind Sthaibhavas run is known as Alambana Vibhavas. The moonlit, spring, soft breeze, fragrance of flowers are Uddipana Vibhavas (stimuli).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing scenes or assessing them, identify both the object/subject of emotion (alambana) and environmental or sensory stimulants (uddipana) that trigger the dominant mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anubhavas (expressive effects / visible signs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anubhavas are their effect seen upon the character after the emotions arise in the actor(s). They make spectators feel or experience Abhinaya by words and gestures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate acting/writing by the clarity and verisimilitude of anubhavas — the bodily/linguistic expressions that communicate internal states to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vyabhikaribhavas (transitory and temporary mental states)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vyabhikaribhavas are the transitory and temporary mental states. They strike mind and become the cause of experiencing a permanent mood. They are 33 in numbers (some examples: weakness, depression, anxiety, despair). They spring out of principal emotion and ultimately merge into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fleeting, contrasting emotions to give depth and movement to a dominant mood; these 'waves and bubbles' enliven the Sthaibhava and help the audience reach Rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realization of Rasa as union of components
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Bharatmuni, the realization of Rasa results from the Union of Vibhavas, Anubhavas, and Vyabhikaribhavas. When Sthaibhavas unite with others, the three Bhavas, one attains the quality of Rasa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rasa is not a single element but the emergent result of Situation (Vibhava) + Expression (Anubhava) + Transitory states (Vyabhikaribhava) centered on a dominant mood (Sthaibhava). Craft scenes so these elements cohere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art vs real-life experience (Rasa's special domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasa theory draws a clear distinction between real-life experience and art experience — unordinary. Rasa is not experienced in common situations but only in the art form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audience requires an adequate degree of intellectual and emotional equipment to realize Rasa; creating Rasa depends on aesthetic framing, not mere replication of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shringara Rasa (erotic / romantic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shringara Rasa: Sthaibhava or emotion of this erotic sentiment is Rati or love. Hero and heroine are Alambana Vibhavas. Swan, youth, solitude, songs of cuckoo are Uddipana Vibhavas. Sideglances, twisting of limbs, brows are Anubhavas. Leaving aside, the fight is Vyabhikaribhvas. Collectively they provide joy Shringara Rasa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To evoke Shringara, combine the dominant mood of love with appropriate beloved-figures (alambana), sensitizing stimuli (uddipana), precise expressive signs (anubhava), and suitable transitory states — all calibrated to produce aesthetic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karuna Rasa (pathos / grief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Karuna Rasa emerges due to Soka (grief). It is pleasurable as it has the power to meet the human heart. A deceased person is Alambana. Reference to him is Uddipana. Cursing destiny, stupefaction are the Anubhavas. Disgust, anxiety and uneasiness are Vyabhikaribhavas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design situations and expressions that foreground loss and grief while using supportive transitory states to deepen the audience's compassionate pleasure in the pathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hasya Rasa (comic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hasya Rasa: the comic elements. It happens by showing unseemly dress, ornaments, quarrels, defective limbs etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic effect arises from highlighting incongruity and social or physical oddities; appropriate expressive signs and stimuli should be used to elicit laughter as an aesthetic response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rudra Rasa (anger / violent passion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rudra Rasa: Anger, rape, abuse, insult, threatening, jealousy etc are Alambana Vibhavas. Beating, breaking, crushing, cutting are Uddipana Vibhavas. Red eyes, knitting of eyebrows, biting of lips, determination, energy, restlessness and trembling are Vyabhikari Bhavas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce the Rudra Rasa, stage or narrate situations and bodily signs indicating violent passion, supported by sensory stimuli and transient states that intensify the dominant anger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other principal Rasas (listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Rasas named: Vira Rasa (zeal or utsaha), Bhayanka Rasa (fear or Bhaya), Adbhuta Rasa (Vismaya), Santa Rasa (Nirveda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed Rasa corresponds to a Sthaibhava/dominant mood (e.g., zeal, fear, wonder, peacefulness). Use the same Vibhava-Anubhava-Vyabhikaribhava framework to construct or evaluate scenes evoking these emotions.
